rounds.text: Crescentis Capital Ltd is currently undergoing a significant operational turnaround, evidenced by a 123% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E18]. This momentum is further validated by the fact that profit growth is currently exceeding one-year price growth by 134%, suggesting the market has yet to fully price in the company's improving earnings profile [E39]. Management confidence is at a multi-year high, with promoters increasing their stake from 69.36% to 74.98% since December 2023 [E33]. The company maintains a lean capital structure with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x [E30] and trades at a significant discount to its sector peers with a price-to-book ratio of 0.23x compared to the 1.25x benchmark [E7]. While the company is expected to deliver a good quarter [E41], it is important to note that the stock is currently trading near the bottom of its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow [E28], a high P/E ratio of 130 [E1], and a poor five-year sales growth record of -22% [E15].

Crescentis Capital Ltd presents a precarious valuation profile, trading at a P/E of 130x [E1] while failing to generate any dividend yield for shareholders [E4]. The company’s fundamental performance is deeply concerning, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of -348% [E17] and a five-year compounded sales growth of -22% [E15]. Operational efficiency is deteriorating, as evidenced by a negative return on equity of -4.8% [E13] and a negative return on capital employed of -4.9% [E12]. Furthermore, the company is burning cash, with operating cash flow and free cash flow both reaching Rs -44.17 Cr and Rs -44.31 Cr respectively in March 2026 [E28, E29]. A discounted cash flow analysis suggests the current market price of Rs 85.4 significantly exceeds the intrinsic value of Rs 15, resulting in a margin of safety of -470.4% [E35, E36]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong promoter holding of 74.98% [E33] and has demonstrated a 123% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E18].

The bear’s focus on a 130x P/E [E1] ignores that the company is currently in a high-growth earnings phase where profit growth is accelerating [E49], making trailing metrics poor indicators of future potential. While the bear highlights negative cash flow [E28, E29], it fails to acknowledge that the company is fundamentally well-positioned with a conservative capital structure and a current ratio of 170.71x [E30, E31]. Conceded: the company has delivered poor sales growth over the past five years [E15, E42] and currently offers no dividend yield [E4]. However, the bear’s reliance on a DCF model [E35, E36] is contradicted by the reality that the company is actively outperforming expectations, with profit growth exceeding one-year price growth by 134% [E39]. The significant increase in promoter holding to 74.98% [E33] signals strong internal confidence in a turnaround, which is further supported by the company being flagged for an expected good quarter [E41]. Finally, the bear’s emphasis on historical ROE [E13] overlooks the current momentum, as the company has achieved 123% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E18, E46].

The bull’s reliance on "accelerating" profit growth [E49] ignores the reality that this growth is occurring against a backdrop of catastrophic sales performance, including a 348% decline in trailing twelve-month sales [E17] and a 22% contraction over five years [E15, E42]. While the bull cites a high current ratio [E31], this figure is dated to 2019 and fails to account for the severe liquidity crisis evidenced by the negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -44.17 Cr and Rs -44.31 Cr respectively in 2026 [E28, E29]. Conceded: promoter holdings have increased to 74.98% [E33]. However, this internal confidence is contradicted by the market’s valuation, which demands an unsustainable 34.4% earnings growth rate just to justify the current price [E37]. The bull’s dismissal of the DCF model [E35, E36] ignores that the company’s own fundamental efficiency metrics, such as a negative ROCE of -4.9% [E12] and a negative ROE of -4.8% [E13], provide no support for the current 130x P/E valuation [E1]. Finally, the claim of momentum is undermined by the fact that working capital days have ballooned from 87.3 to 170, signaling significant operational inefficiency [E44].
